name: metre
definition: The metre, symbol m, is the SI unit of length. It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the speed of light in vacuum c to be 299 792 458 when expressed in the unit m/s, where the second is defined in terms of the caesium frequency ΔνCs.

name: second
definition: The second, symbol s, is the SI unit of time. It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the caesium frequency ΔνCs, the unperturbed ground-state hyperfine transition frequency of the caesium-133 atom, to be 9 192 631 770 when expressed in the unit Hz, which is equal to s⁻¹.

name: kilogram
definition: The kilogram, symbol kg, is the SI unit of mass. It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the Planck constant h to be 6.626 070 15 × 10⁻³⁴ when expressed in the unit J s, which is equal to kg m² s⁻¹, where the metre and the second are defined in terms of c and ΔνCs.

name: ampere
definition: The ampere, symbol A, is the SI unit of electric current. It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the elementary charge e to be 1.602 176 634 × 10⁻¹⁹ when expressed in the unit C, which is equal to A s, where the second is defined in terms of ΔνCs.

name: kelvin
definition: The kelvin, symbol K, is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature. It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the Boltzmann constant k to be 1.380 649 × 10⁻²³ when expressed in the unit J K⁻¹, which is equal to kg m² s⁻² K⁻¹, where the kilogram, metre and second are defined in terms of h, c and ΔνCs.

name: mole
definition: The mole, symbol mol, is the SI unit of amount of substance. One mole contains exactly 6.022 140 76 × 10²³ elementary entities. This number is the fixed numerical value of the Avogadro constant N_A when expressed in the unit mol⁻¹ and is called the Avogadro number.

name: candela
definition: The candela, symbol cd, is the SI unit of luminous intensity in a given direction. It is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the luminous efficacy of monochromatic radiation of frequency 540 × 10¹² Hz, K_cd, to be 683 when expressed in the unit lm W⁻¹, which is equal to cd sr W⁻¹, or cd sr kg⁻¹ m⁻² s³, where the kilogram, metre and second are defined in terms of h, c and ΔνCs.

name: radian
definition: The radian is the coherent derived unit for plane angle. One radian is the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc that is equal in length to the radius.

name: steradian
definition: The steradian is the coherent derived unit for solid angle. One steradian is the solid angle subtended at the centre of a sphere by an area of surface equal to the square of the radius.

name: hertz
definition: The hertz is the unit of frequency. One hertz is one cycle per second.

name: newton
definition: The newton is the unit of force. One newton is the force that gives to a mass of one kilogram an acceleration of one metre per second squared.

name: pascal
definition: The pascal is the unit of pressure and stress. One pascal is one newton per square metre.

name: joule
definition: The joule is the unit of energy, work and amount of heat. One joule is the work done when a force of one newton moves its point of application by one metre.

name: watt
definition: The watt is the unit of power and radiant flux. One watt is one joule per second.

name: coulomb
definition: The coulomb is the unit of electric charge. One coulomb is the charge transported by a current of one ampere in one second.

name: volt
definition: The volt is the unit of electric potential difference and electromotive force. One volt is the potential difference between two points of a conducting wire carrying a constant current of one ampere when the power dissipated between these points is one watt.

name: farad
definition: The farad is the unit of capacitance. One farad is the capacitance of a capacitor between whose plates a potential difference of one volt appears when it is charged with one coulomb.

name: ohm
definition: The ohm is the unit of electric resistance. One ohm is the resistance between two points of a conductor when a potential difference of one volt produces a current of one ampere.

name: siemens
definition: The siemens is the unit of electric conductance. One siemens is the conductance of a conductor in which a current of one ampere is produced by a potential difference of one volt.

name: weber
definition: The weber is the unit of magnetic flux. One weber is the magnetic flux which, linking a circuit of one turn, produces in it an electromotive force of one volt as it is reduced to zero in one second.

name: tesla
definition: The tesla is the unit of magnetic flux density. One tesla is one weber per square metre.

name: henry
definition: The henry is the unit of inductance. One henry is the inductance of a closed circuit in which an electromotive force of one volt is produced when the electric current in the circuit varies uniformly at a rate of one ampere per second.

name: degree Celsius
definition: The degree Celsius is the unit of Celsius temperature. It is equal in magnitude to the kelvin: t/°C = T/K − 273.15, where t is the Celsius temperature and T the thermodynamic temperature.

name: lumen
definition: The lumen is the unit of luminous flux. One lumen is the luminous flux emitted in a unit solid angle by a point source of luminous intensity one candela.

name: lux
definition: The lux is the unit of illuminance. One lux is one lumen per square metre.

name: becquerel
definition: The becquerel is the unit of activity referred to a radionuclide. One becquerel is the activity of a quantity of radioactive material in which one nucleus decays per second.

name: gray
quantity: absorbed dose, kerma, specific energy imparted
definition: The gray is the unit of absorbed dose, kerma and specific energy imparted. One gray is one joule per kilogram.

name: sievert
definition: The sievert is the unit of dose equivalent and of the quantities derived from it. One sievert is one joule per kilogram.

name: katal
definition: The katal is the unit of catalytic activity. One katal is the catalytic activity of a catalyst that converts one mole of substrate per second.
